person: Grace Lindqvist is a 59-year-old retired librarian who lives three states from where her parents did. Her mother died this month and she is the court-appointed representative of the estate. Two years ago she paid for her father's funeral and burial out of her own pocket. He was a Vietnam-era Army veteran, and no one told her the VA might repay part of it. She is tired and grieving, uses a laptop slowly, and wants one gentle step at a time. She has just learned the VA may have a deadline she is close to missing.
stated_up_front: I'm sorry to bother you, there is so much this week. My mother just died, and a friend said the VA might have paid something toward my father's burial two years ago, which I paid myself. Could you look and see whether there is anything still owed, and tell me what you need from me?

facts.truth: Walter Lindqvist, U.S. Army, served 1967 to 1969, honorable discharge on his DD-214.

facts.about: Date of his death and burial
facts.truth: He died at home on November 4, 2024 and was buried on November 9, 2024, so the two years end November 9, 2026.
Pancreatic cancer, at home under a private hospice, not in a VA hospital or VA care.
A 2019 rating decision gave him 70 percent for hearing loss and PTSD, paid at the 100 percent rate through unemployability. The cancer was not among the rated conditions.

facts.about: What she paid the funeral home
facts.truth: $8,940 final statement from the funeral home, paid in full with her own card in November 2024.
$1,350 for the lot and $1,100 for opening and closing the grave, paid by check from her own account.
No one has repaid her anything, not her siblings, her mother, or his estate.
Her father is in the Garden of Rest section of Maple Hill Cemetery. Her sister's note says that section allows only flat bronze markers, and there is no headstone on the grave yet.
The funeral home's catalog offered a granite marker for about $1,200. She has not bought it.
A company that emailed her offered to file the claim for $395. She has not answered.
Her brother Peter and her sister Annika want things finished fairly. Annika wrote the note in the family folder.

unknowns: Whether the VA calls her father's death service-connected, and what the unemployability rating means for that
The exact dollar amounts the VA pays for the date of death, for either the burial allowance or the plot allowance
Whether a bronze marker or a medallion is the right kind for a grave with no headstone
Whether the two-year deadline applies to the plot allowance and the marker as well
